newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees turnaround in global electronics.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees turnaround in global electronics.

text.p: Turnaround in global electronics demand has begun and is likely to continue in the coming months, Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Monday.
"However, competition in the industry is likely to intensify. This will exert downward pressure on prices of key electronic products, resulting in a squeeze in profit margin."
TDB said this was evident in the decline in prices of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips by about 29 percent since March 1997.
Similiarly, major manufacturers of personal computers have been slashing prices to maintain market share in highly competitive markets.
"On balance, TDB's assessment is that the earlier projected total trade growth of five to seven percent for 1997 would be achieved," it said.
